one_liner: C++ text retrieval and analysis toolkit; its ACL 2016 demo paper reports faster indexing than Lucene and Indri and faster linear classification than LIBLINEAR.
what_it_does: MeTA (ModErn Text Analysis) is a research and teaching toolkit from UIUC that bundles tokenizers and analyzers, on-disk inverted and forward indexes, rankers (BM25, language-model smoothing and others), classifiers, topic models, language models, a CRF tagger and parsers in one C++ codebase, configured through TOML files. It is not a drop-in for Lucene or Indri: you describe a corpus (line, gzipped line, libsvm and other formats) and analyzers in config.toml and use MeTA's own index, ranker and classifier classes. Python bindings exist as metapy on PyPI (last release 0.2.13, 2018-08-06).
how_it_is_fast: Indexing tokenizes documents on all hardware threads by default (indexer-num-threads). Each thread fills a RAM-budgeted in-memory chunk (a hash probe_set of postings buffers) and flushes it to disk, with up to 8 concurrent writers. The chunks are then combined by an external multiway merge, and a compression pass writes gap-encoded postings in 7-bit variable-byte form plus a memory-mapped, B+-tree-like vocabulary map. Classification uses SGD with the normalized adaptive gradient (NAG) method of Ross, Mineiro and Langford, L2 regularization via the scalar-times-vector trick and L1 via Tsuruoka's cumulative penalty, and it can stream mini-batches from the index instead of loading the whole dataset like LIBLINEAR.
when_to_use: Research or coursework that needs search, text analysis, classification and topic models over the same index in one C++ (or Python, via metapy) toolkit.

Building an inverted index over a multi-gigabyte static collection on a multicore machine, where MeTA's parallel chunked indexer is reported to finish Gov2 in about 1h12m versus about 8h for Indri (snippet-only figures).
Linear text classification (SVM or logistic loss via SGD) on sparse bag-of-words features where a few passes of online SGD are accurate enough and LIBLINEAR's exact solver is slower.
Training on datasets larger than RAM: the project's tutorial trains an SGD SVM on about 1.2 GB of rcv1.binary data in mini-batches with a 128 MB maximum resident set.
when_not_to_use: Production search services: there is no query server, replication, near-real-time updates or a published query-throughput comparison. The snippets say retrieval speed was roughly even with Lucene and Indri.
Anything needing maintenance: master was last changed 2017-08-20 (v3.0.2), develop in 2018, and 50 issues are open, including unanswered build failures and a segfault (#209).

Modern toolchains out of the box: CMake requires exactly ICU 58.2 and otherwise tries to download it from download.icu-project.org, which no longer serves it (issue #216, open since 2020-05-13). Windows is documented only for MinGW-w64 under MSYS2 (no MSVC guide, and ICU auto-build refuses non-MinGW Windows).
Exact (non-SGD) SVM or logistic-regression solutions: MeTA's speed advantage over LIBLINEAR comes from running a different, approximate algorithm.
32-bit targets: support is best-effort because the indexes rely heavily on memory mapping.

integration.form: libraries built with CMake (meta-index, meta-utf and others, plus command-line tools), or the metapy Python wheel
integration.dependencies: ICU (exactly 58.2, else built from source), zlib, threads; optional liblzma and jemalloc; git submodules (cpptoml, meta-cmake and others)
integration.min_toolchain: C++14 as set in CMakeLists (the code claims C++11); Travis CI covered GCC 4.8 to 5 and Clang, README guides go up to GCC 5.3; the last fixes target GCC 7.1.1 (2017)
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows via MinGW-w64/MSYS2 only; 64-bit strongly recommended
integration.thread_safety: not documented for concurrent use of an index; indexing and some algorithms are internally multithreaded

gotchas: The only speed numbers come from the authors' ACL 2016 demo paper, which was never opened here (all ACL Anthology hosts are blocked). The Blog06/Lucene indexing figures rest on a single garbled search snippet. Hardware, compiler, thread counts and Lucene, Indri and LIBLINEAR versions are all unknown, and MeTA's indexer uses every hardware thread by default.

The record's 'LIBLINEAR killed while loading' evidence is from the online-learning tutorial, which uses rcv1.binary with the splits reversed (about 1.2 GB of training data, run in mini-batches of 50,000 documents on a machine with about 200 MB of RAM), not Webspam. The tutorial itself says the dataset 'is not actually large enough to require an online learning algorithm'.

The 20news comparison pits SGD (an approximate online method) against LIBLINEAR's exact solver. The roughly 4x time gap (0.648 s vs 2.58 s, IO excluded) reflects the algorithm choice, not a faster implementation of the same solver.

Building from a clean checkout usually fails at the ICU step: FindOrBuildICU accepts only ICU 58.2, and any other system version triggers a download from a dead URL. Users report fixing it by pointing the URL in CMakeLists.txt at the unicode-org/icu GitHub release (issue #216, no maintainer reply).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick MeTA over Tantivy, PISA, IResearch or SeekStorm only when you want search plus text mining (classifiers, topic models, language models, parsers) over one index for research or teaching. For query throughput or production indexing, those siblings are maintained and have current independent search-benchmark-game numbers against Lucene, while MeTA has none.
verified_claims_summary: These are first-party figures from the authors' ACL 2016 system-demonstration paper, seen only through search snippets. Index build time was Gov2 about 1h12m vs about 2h vs about 8h14m and Blog06 11m23s vs 20m23s vs 55m40s for MeTA vs Lucene vs Indri (Blog06 uncorroborated). Linear classification on 20news reached 80.1% in 0.648 s vs LIBLINEAR's 79.4% in 2.58 s, and on Webspam MeTA finished in 1m16s where LIBLINEAR ran out of memory. Hardware, compiler, thread counts and baseline versions are unknown, and no benchmark code is public.
status_note: Abandoned since 2017-08-20 (v3.0.2; develop last touched 2018) with 50 open issues and no maintainer replies on build breakages; MIT/NCSA-licensed and usable for teaching and research if you pin ICU 58.2 and an older GCC or Clang.
